definition: A graph-structured representation of knowledge consisting of entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges), used to organize and query structured information.
details: Knowledge graphs are used both as a data source for retrieval-augmented systems (as in GraphRAG) and as a target for information extraction tasks, where a model extracts entities and relations from unstructured text.

explainer.lead: A knowledge graph stores knowledge as entities (nodes) joined by typed relationships (edges), giving a structure that can be organised and queried. It matters as both a retrieval source for systems like GraphRAG and a target for extracting facts from text.

tiers.eli5: It is a web of named things connected by labelled arrows, like a map where every line says how its two places are related.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use graphs as a retrieval source in GraphRAG pipelines and as the output structure for entity and relation extraction from unstructured text. The pitfall is schema and entity-resolution debt: duplicate nodes and sloppy relation types quietly ruin retrieval quality.
tiers.paperLevel: A graph G = (V, E) where nodes V are entities and edges E are typed relations between them, queried with graph or triple patterns; coverage and consistency depend entirely on how it was built.

explainer.example: A query asks which companies share a board member with a given firm; the graph traverses person-company edges to return the answer in one hop pattern.
